usageNotes: Use this to apply pending container configuration changes (e.g. CPU, memory, network edits) without a full stop/start cycle; Proxmox performs a clean shutdown then immediately starts the container again. The container must be in a running state and the target node must be online; calling this on a stopped container will fail. Returns a task UPID string — poll the node's task log to confirm completion.

examples.summary: Reboot LXC container 110 on node pve1 with a 60-second shutdown timeout

destructiveReason: Rebooting the container interrupts all running services inside it for the duration of the shutdown and startup cycle.
tips: If timeout is omitted, Proxmox uses its default shutdown timeout (typically 60 s); set an explicit value for containers with slow-stopping services.
The returned UPID can be passed to GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to monitor reboot progress.
Pending config changes saved via PUT /nodes/{node}/lxc/{vmid}/config are applied automatically during the reboot without needing a separate commit step.
